_comment: Single source of defaults for stackup, materials and fabrication limits. Read by the solver app and the plugin; the user can override any value (see docs/PLAN.md, Defaults and editable attributes). Lengths in millimetres here for readability; the core converts to SI at load. 'source' says where each number comes from; 'assumed' marks values no fab publishes. Each profile's 'dielectrics' lists its dielectric layers top to bottom (copper is a zero-thickness sheet between them in the model); a value named in a layer's 'assumed' list is not published by the fab (the 'source' says where it comes from). Profiles are for a given copper-layer count; the solver applies one only to a board with that many copper layers.

fr4.source: assumed generic FR-4 (neither fab publishes a general value): er 4.5, tan d 0.02; the fab profiles carry laminate-specific values where a datasheet gives them

fr408.source: Isola FR408HR datasheet rev C (linked from https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/): Dk 3.72/3.69/3.68/3.64/3.65 and Df 0.0072/0.0091/0.0092/0.0098/0.0095 at 100 MHz/1/2/5/10 GHz (1 GHz values used)

copper.source: assumed: bulk annealed copper; real PCB copper is lower (roughness)

dielectrics.name: core
dielectrics.source: https://docs.oshpark.com/services/two-layer/ stackup table (60 mil core); Dk and Df from the Kingboard KB-6167F datasheet (linked from https://docs.oshpark.com/services/two-layer/), typical, IPC-TM-650 2.5.5.2: Dk 4.8 at 1 MHz and 4.6 at 1 GHz, Df 0.015 at 1 MHz and 0.016 at 1 GHz (1 GHz values used, nearest the radio bands). The OSH Park page itself says Dk 4.5 at 10 MHz and publishes no Df.

oshpark_4layer.source: https://docs.oshpark.com/services/ read 2026-11-19; https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer re-read 2026-11-23: stackup table lists the outer layers as 1 oz copper clad+plated, 1.7 mil (43.2 um), the inner layers as 0.5 oz copper clad, 0.68 mil (17.5 um); rows sum to 61.9 mil against a stated 63 mil nominal; the page has a changelog line (28-JAN-2026) about a temporary alternate stackup for some 4-layer orders that is not described in the page body, so a real board may differ
oshpark_4layer.name: OSH Park 4-layer, ENIG, FR408HR

dielectrics.name: prepreg 2113
dielectrics.source: https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/ (7.87 mil 2113 prepreg, Dk 3.61 at 1 GHz); Df 0.0091 is the FR408HR laminate's at 1 GHz from the datasheet (prepreg-specific Df not published): Isola FR408HR datasheet rev C (linked from https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/): Dk 3.72/3.69/3.68/3.64/3.65 and Df 0.0072/0.0091/0.0092/0.0098/0.0095 at 100 MHz/1/2/5/10 GHz (1 GHz values used)

dielectrics.name: core
dielectrics.source: https://docs.oshpark.com/resources/four-layer-stackup.png (OSH Park's stackup diagram, read 2026-11-23): core FR408HR 39.0 mil, Dk 3.87, Df 0.009; the page text of https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer gives no core Dk, and the Isola FR408HR datasheet rev C gives 3.69 at 1 GHz (used until 2026-11-23; the fab's own figure is used now)

dielectrics.name: prepreg 2113
dielectrics.source: https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/ (7.87 mil 2113 prepreg, Dk 3.61 at 1 GHz); Df 0.0091 is the FR408HR laminate's at 1 GHz from the datasheet (prepreg-specific Df not published): Isola FR408HR datasheet rev C (linked from https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/): Dk 3.72/3.69/3.68/3.64/3.65 and Df 0.0072/0.0091/0.0092/0.0098/0.0095 at 100 MHz/1/2/5/10 GHz (1 GHz values used)

dielectrics.name: core
dielectrics.source: https://docs.oshpark.com/services/six-layer/ (36.44 mil FR408HR core; the page gives no core Dk or Df); values from the Isola FR408HR datasheet rev C (linked from https://docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/): Dk 3.72/3.69/3.68/3.64/3.65 and Df 0.0072/0.0091/0.0092/0.0098/0.0095 at 100 MHz/1/2/5/10 GHz (1 GHz values used)

pcbway_2layer.source: https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html read 2026-11-19 (standard tier; the advanced tier allows tighter limits)
pcbway_2layer.name: PCBWay 2-layer, ENIG, FR4

dielectrics.name: core
dielectrics.source: derived: 1.6 mm finished thickness less two 35 um copper layers; PCBWay publishes no 2-layer stackup, so the core Dk 4.6 is the value its 4-layer table gives for cores (https://www.pcbway.com/multi-layer-laminated-structure.html); loss tangent not published by PCBWay: assumed 0.016, the Kingboard KB-6167F figure at 1 GHz (one of PCBWay's listed FR4 materials; S1141 blog figures are 0.015 to 0.017). Manufacturer datasheet for the material actually used was not read

pcbway_4layer.source: https://www.pcbway.com/multi-layer-laminated-structure.html entry 1 (4 layers, 1.6 mm, outer 0.5 oz base plated to 1 oz, inner 1 oz, 70% residual copper) read 2026-11-20; limits as pcbway_2layer
pcbway_4layer.name: PCBWay 4-layer, ENIG, FR4

dielectrics.name: prepreg 7628
dielectrics.source: https://www.pcbway.com/multi-layer-laminated-structure.html entry 1 (laminated thickness 0.1855 mm, Dk 4.74, no frequency stated); loss tangent not published by PCBWay: assumed 0.016, the Kingboard KB-6167F figure at 1 GHz (one of PCBWay's listed FR4 materials; S1141 blog figures are 0.015 to 0.017). Manufacturer datasheet for the material actually used was not read

dielectrics.name: core
dielectrics.source: https://www.pcbway.com/multi-layer-laminated-structure.html entry 1 (1.03 mm, Core DK 4.6, no frequency stated); loss tangent not published by PCBWay: assumed 0.016, the Kingboard KB-6167F figure at 1 GHz (one of PCBWay's listed FR4 materials; S1141 blog figures are 0.015 to 0.017). Manufacturer datasheet for the material actually used was not read

dielectrics.name: prepreg 7628
dielectrics.source: https://www.pcbway.com/multi-layer-laminated-structure.html entry 1 (as above); loss tangent not published by PCBWay: assumed 0.016, the Kingboard KB-6167F figure at 1 GHz (one of PCBWay's listed FR4 materials; S1141 blog figures are 0.015 to 0.017). Manufacturer datasheet for the material actually used was not read

common_denominator.source: the limits both fabs can build: used for the W3008 reference board and as the default when no profile is chosen
common_denominator.name: Common limits, 2-layer FR4 (default)

dielectrics.name: core
dielectrics.source: assumed: 1.6 mm board less two 35 um copper layers; FR-4 values as in materials.fr4

defaults.source: profile: our choice; boundary distance: assumption to be confirmed by convergence tests

_note_pcbway_layers: PCBWay's page counts 4-layer stackups (112 of 298 entries) but the 6-layer and larger tables could not be read (2026-11-20; its 6-layer example is an image), so there is no 6-layer or larger PCBWay profile; PCBWay publishes no 2-layer stackup (its stock 1.6 mm board uses a 1.2 mm core with 18/35/70 um copper per the cores table at /pcb_prototype/Cost_cores_Foil___Prepreg_for_PCBs.html, not labelled 2-layer), no Df, and no Dk frequency. ENIG ('Immersion gold' and 'ENIG') is listed in its standard and advanced finishes with no layer-count restriction (capabilities.html, /pcb_prototype/Comparison_of_several_PCB_surface_finish_types.html).
